chunks: The Sheikh, the jurist, Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babawayh al-Qummi (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Yahya al-Attar narrated to us from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Isa from al-Hasan b. Mahbub from Abu Ayyub from Abu al-Ward from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him). He said:

The Messenger of Allah (may Allah's blessings be upon him and his family) delivered a sermon to the people on the last Friday of Sha'ban. He praised and commended Allah, then said: O people! A month has shaded you containing a night better than a thousand months; it is the month of Ramadan. Allah has obligated its fasting and made voluntary prayer in one of its nights equivalent to seventy nights of voluntary prayer in other months. He has made a voluntary good deed therein like the reward of one who performed an obligation of Allah's obligations, and whoever performs an obligation therein, it is as if he performed seventy obligations in other months. It is the month of patience, and the reward of patience is Paradise. It is the month of sympathy. It is a month in which Allah increases the sustenance of the believer. Whoever feeds a fasting believer therein, it will be for him with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, the freeing of a slave and forgiveness for his past sins.

So it was said to him: O Messenger of Allah! Not all of us can feed a fasting person. He said: Indeed Allah, blessed and exalted, is generous. He gives this reward to those of you who cannot manage more than a sip of milk to feed a fasting person, or a drink of fresh water, or some small dates. And whoever lightens the burden on his servant therein, Allah will lighten his reckoning. It is a month whose beginning is mercy, its middle is forgiveness, and its end is the answering of prayers and freedom from the Fire. You cannot do without four traits therein: two with which you please Allah, and two you cannot do without. As for the two with which you please Allah: it is the testimony that there is no god but Allah and that I am the Messenger of Allah. As for the two you cannot do without: you ask Allah for your needs and Paradise, and you ask Allah for well-being therein and seek refuge in Him from the Fire.

key_terms.العتق من النار: Freedom from the Fire — divine emancipation from hellfire during Ramadan
key_terms.المواساة: Sympathy/consolation — caring for and supporting fellow believers
key_terms.شهر الصبر: The month of patience — a designation for Ramadan emphasizing its spiritual discipline
key_terms.ليلة القدر: The Night of Decree — a night in Ramadan better than a thousand months (Quran 97:3)

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about Ramadan in his sermon on the last Friday of Sha'ban?
ai.summary: The Prophet's sermon on the last Friday of Sha'ban about the virtues of Ramadan. He describes it as a month containing a night better than a thousand months (Laylat al-Qadr), where voluntary worship equals seventy nights elsewhere and obligatory acts equal seventy obligations in other months. It is the month of patience (whose reward is Paradise), sympathy, and increased provision. He encourages feeding the fasting and lightening the burden on servants. The month's beginning is mercy, its middle is forgiveness, and its end is answering of prayers and freedom from the Fire. He concludes with four essential traits: testifying to God's oneness and the Prophet's mission, and asking Allah for one's needs and refuge from the Fire.

en.bilal-muhammad: Abu Ja`far Muhammad b. `Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babuwayh al-Qummi (rh) narrated to us. He said: My father (rh) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Yahya al-`Attar narrated to us from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. `Isa from al-Hasan b. Mahbub from Abi Ayyub from Abi’l Ward from Abi Ja`far (as). He said:

The Messenger of Allah (s) delivered a sermon to the people on the last Friday of Sha`ban. He praised and commended Allah, then said: O people! You are shaded by a month wherein there is a night that is better than one thousand months – and it is the month of Ramadan. Allah has obligated fasting it, and He has made voluntary prayer therein equivalent to seventy nights of voluntary prayers in other months. For those who pray voluntarily therein, He has given them goodness; like the reward of one who has performed a divinely mandated obligatory act. Whoever performs a divinely mandated obligatory act therein, it will be equivalent to one who performs seventy obligatory acts in other months. It is the month of patience, and whoever is patient, his reward is Paradise. It is the month of sympathy. It is a month in which Allah increases the sustenance of the believer. Whoever feeds a fasting believer therein, Allah will free his neck [from the Fire] and forgive his past sins.

So, it was said to him: O Messenger of Allah! Not all of us are capable of feeding a fasting person. So, he said: Surely, Allah is generous. He will give this reward to those of you who are not capable of feeding a fasting person anything but watery milk, pure water, or small dates – and not capable of [feeding him] anything more than this. Whoever lightens things for his slaves therein, Allah will lighten his judgment. It is a month in which its beginning is mercy, its middle is forgiveness, and its end is acceptance [of prayers] and freedom from the Fire. There are four things therein that you are not needless of: two that you will please Allah by, and two you absolutely need. As for the two that you will please Allah by: they are the testimony that there is no god but Allah, and that I am the Messenger of Allah. As for the two that you absolutely need: you will ask Allah for your needs and for Paradise, and you will ask Allah therein for His forgiveness and His pardon from the Fire.
